programme.subtitle: Learn how Terraform configuration is formed by building every block yourself.
programme.description: Start with no lab infrastructure. Read HCL, create each project file, add blocks and arguments gradually, evaluate expressions, connect variables, locals, data, resources and outputs, then plan, apply, change and safely destroy a small AWS configuration.
programme.learningOutcome: Read, write, explain and safely operate a complete Terraform root configuration without relying on pasted finished files.

tasks.title: Recognise Terraform blocks, arguments and expressions
tasks.goal: Read small HCL examples and identify what each symbol means before creating infrastructure.
tasks.whyItMatters: A learner who can label the structure can safely edit and troubleshoot Terraform instead of treating configuration as a script to copy.

tasks.whyItMatters: Terraform loads every .tf file in the current directory, so identity, Region and folder mistakes can change the wrong resources.

consoleSteps.title: Prepare the exact training boundary
consoleSteps.instruction: Sign in to the training AWS account as an administrator or approved temporary administrative role; do not use the root user.

instructions.text: Sign in to the training AWS account as an administrator or approved temporary administrative role; do not use the root user.
Open the account menu and record the 12-digit account ID as [ACCOUNT_ID].
Use the Region selector to choose Europe (London) eu-west-2.
Open IAM, choose Policies, choose Create policy, then choose JSON.
Paste the supplied fa-terraform-structure-training-policy JSON.
Replace <ACCOUNT_ID> with the recorded account ID and change nothing else.
Choose Next and name it fa-terraform-structure-training-policy.
Have an administrator review the exact actions and /fa-terraform-structure/* resource boundary before creating it.
Attach it only to an approved temporary role or the temporary user fa-terraform-structure-user.
If local credentials are required, create one access key for that temporary identity and place it only into the protected AWS CLI prompt.
Open CloudShell, or open PowerShell on the local computer.
Create a folder named fa-terraform-structure using the command for the selected terminal.
Enter that folder and display its full path.
List its contents and remove nothing; if old .tf or state files exist, stop and use a new empty folder.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The terminal is inside one empty fa-terraform-structure folder and the caller is a non-root approved training identity.

tasks.title: Build terraform and provider blocks gradually
tasks.goal: Create the first two files by adding and explaining one block at a time.
tasks.whyItMatters: Version constraints protect compatibility, while provider configuration tells Terraform which plugin and AWS context to use.
requiredPermissions: Use only the approved fa-terraform-structure training identity and exact /fa-terraform-structure/* parameter path.

console.reason: Complete editor and AWS Console guidance is included.

cli.reason: Complete Terraform and AWS CLI guidance is included.

consoleSteps.title: Construct versions.tf
consoleSteps.instruction: Create an empty file named versions.tf in the project folder.

instructions.text: Create an empty file named versions.tf in the project folder.
Type terraform followed by an opening brace, press Enter, then add the matching closing brace.
Inside that body, add required_version = ">= 1.10.0".
Explain that required_version constrains Terraform CLI, not the AWS provider.
Inside the terraform body, add the required_providers block.
Inside required_providers, add the aws block with source and version arguments exactly as supplied.
Explain that source selects the provider and version constrains compatible releases.
Save versions.tf, compare it with the finished reference, then run terraform fmt.
Run terraform init and identify the new .terraform directory and .terraform.lock.hcl file.
Explain that the lock file records selected provider versions and should normally be committed, while .terraform should not.

jsonBlocks.title: Finished versions.tf reference

consoleSteps.expectedResult: versions.tf is formatted, the AWS provider initializes and the dependency lock file exists.

consoleSteps.title: Construct providers.tf
consoleSteps.instruction: Create an empty file named providers.tf.

instructions.text: Create an empty file named providers.tf.
Add provider "aws" followed by an opening and closing brace.
Explain that aws is the provider’s local name in this configuration.
Inside the block, add region = var.aws_region.
Add profile = var.aws_profile on the next line.
Notice that var.aws_region and var.aws_profile are references, not quoted text.
Save the file and run terraform fmt.
Run terraform validate and read the errors about undeclared variables; this is expected because the referenced variable blocks do not exist yet.
Do not replace the references with hard-coded values; the next task will declare them.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: providers.tf contains two variable references and the learner understands why validation is not complete yet.
consoleSteps.warning: The temporary validation error is intentional and is resolved in the next task.

cliSteps.explanation: Format the new Terraform block.
Install the constrained AWS provider and create its lock file.
See which provider the root configuration requires.
Format providers.tf after adding the provider block.
Observe the useful undeclared-variable errors before the variables are added.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Terraform names aws_region and aws_profile as undeclared input variables.

verification.title: Explain both version constraints
verification.instruction: Describe the difference between required_version and required_providers.aws.version.
verification.expectedResult: The learner distinguishes Terraform CLI compatibility from provider compatibility.

verification.title: Inspect generated files
verification.instruction: List hidden files and identify .terraform and .terraform.lock.hcl.
verification.expectedResult: The learner knows which generated item is normally committed.

tasks.title: Declare typed input variables and validation
tasks.goal: Replace unexplained hard-coded settings with typed, described and validated inputs.
tasks.whyItMatters: Variables form the input interface to a root module and allow controlled reuse without editing resource blocks.

consoleSteps.title: Construct variables.tf one variable at a time
consoleSteps.instruction: Create an empty file named variables.tf.

instructions.text: Create an empty file named variables.tf.
Add only the aws_region variable block with its description, type and default.
Explain that type = string rejects incompatible values and default makes the variable optional.
Add the validation block inside aws_region.
Explain that condition must be true and error_message tells the learner how to correct an invalid value.
Save, run terraform fmt, then run terraform validate; the aws_profile error should remain.
Add the aws_profile variable block and validate again.
Add the environment variable block and explain how it will later affect names and tags.
Add parameter_values as map(string).
Explain that a map has unique keys and that every value must be a string.
Type the two supplied default map entries carefully, including the comma between entries.
Save, format and validate the complete file.
Compare your file with the finished reference only after it validates.

jsonBlocks.title: Finished variables.tf reference

consoleSteps.expectedResult: variables.tf declares four documented typed inputs and terraform validate succeeds.

consoleSteps.title: Test how variable values enter the configuration
consoleSteps.instruction: Create terraform.tfvars only after understanding the variable defaults.

instructions.text: Create terraform.tfvars only after understanding the variable defaults.
Add environment = "training".
Add the parameter_values map with application, owner and purpose entries.
Explain that terraform.tfvars overrides matching defaults automatically.
Confirm this file contains no password, access key or secret.
Save it and compare it with the supplied reference.
Run terraform validate again.
Run terraform console, evaluate var.environment and then var.parameter_values, and leave with exit.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The learner can explain defaults, overrides, type constraints and validation.

cliSteps.explanation: Format variables.tf after each meaningful addition.

Read the effective environment input.

cliSteps.explanation: Leave the expression console.

verification.title: Explain value precedence used here

tasks.title: Build locals, data and resource references
tasks.goal: Connect inputs to reusable expressions, read the AWS account and create multiple resources from one block.
tasks.whyItMatters: References form Terraform’s dependency graph and expressions let concise configuration represent repeatable infrastructure.
requiredPermissions: Use only the approved fa-terraform-structure training identity and exact /fa-terraform-structure/* parameter path.

cli.reason: Complete Terraform and AWS CLI guidance is included.

consoleSteps.title: Create reusable local values
consoleSteps.instruction: Create locals.tf and add an empty locals block.

instructions.text: Create locals.tf and add an empty locals block.
Add name_prefix = "/fa-terraform-structure/${var.environment}".
Explain that ${var.environment} is string interpolation and will evaluate to training.
Add common_tags as a map containing ManagedBy, FollowAlong and Environment.
Set Environment to var.environment without quotes because it is a reference.
Save, format and validate.
Use terraform console to evaluate local.name_prefix and local.common_tags, then leave the console.

jsonBlocks.title: Finished locals.tf reference

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The local values evaluate to the expected prefix and reusable tag map.

consoleSteps.title: Add a read-only data source

instructions.text: Create data.tf.
Add data "aws_caller_identity" "current" with an empty body.
Explain that data is the block type, aws_caller_identity is the data-source type and current is its local label.
Explain that this reads the current account and does not create or manage the identity.
Save, format and validate.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: data.tf contains one read-only data block.

consoleSteps.title: Construct the managed resource block
consoleSteps.instruction: Create main.tf and add resource "aws_ssm_parameter" "training" with an empty body.

instructions.text: Create main.tf and add resource "aws_ssm_parameter" "training" with an empty body.
Say its Terraform address before instances exist: aws_ssm_parameter.training.
Add for_each = var.parameter_values and explain that Terraform will create one instance per map key.
Add name = "${local.name_prefix}/${each.key}".
Explain that local.name_prefix is reused and each.key is the current map key.
Add description using each.key.
Add type = "String".
Add value = each.value and explain why it is not quoted.
Add tags = local.common_tags.
Save, format and validate.
Compare the complete file with the finished reference only after validation succeeds.

jsonBlocks.title: Finished main.tf reference
jsonBlocks.content:
resource "aws_ssm_parameter" "training" {
  for_each = var.parameter_values

  name        = "${local.name_prefix}/${each.key}"
  description = "Terraform structure lesson value for ${each.key}"
  type        = "String"
  value       = each.value
  tags        = local.common_tags
}

consoleSteps.expectedResult: One resource block describes three separately addressed Parameter Store parameters.

cliSteps.explanation: Format each new file after a meaningful block is complete.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Terraform reports changed filenames only when formatting was needed.

cliSteps.explanation: Validate all files as one configuration.
Open the expression console.
Evaluate a local derived from an input variable.
Evaluate the reusable tags map.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Terraform displays the three expected tags.

cliSteps.explanation: Inspect the keys that for_each will use.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Terraform lists application, owner and purpose.

cliSteps.explanation: Leave the expression console.

verification.expectedResult: The name becomes /fa-terraform-structure/training/application and the value becomes study-tracker.

verification.title: Explain dependency information

Add output "parameter_names" with an empty body.
Add its description argument.
Add value = values(aws_ssm_parameter.training)[*].name.

Explain that [*].name selects the name attribute from every instance.
Add output "verified_account_id".
Set its value to data.aws_caller_identity.current.account_id.
Trace the reference as block type, data-source type, local label and exported attribute.

consoleSteps.title: Rebuild the mental model
consoleSteps.instruction: Without opening the finished references, write the seven filenames used by the project.

instructions.text: Without opening the finished references, write the seven filenames used by the project.
Beside versions.tf, write Terraform CLI and provider constraints.
Beside providers.tf, write AWS Region and profile configuration.
Beside variables.tf, write typed external inputs and validation.
Beside locals.tf, write reusable internal expressions.
Beside data.tf, write read existing information without managing it.
Beside main.tf, write managed resources and their desired settings.
Beside outputs.tf, write useful exported attributes.
Explain that Terraform combines all .tf files in the directory regardless of filename order.
Explain the sequence fmt, init, validate, plan, apply and destroy in your own words.
